reason: This passage (Exodus 3-4) describes God commissioning Moses and Aaron to communicate with the Hebrew people about their deliverance from Egypt. The text emphasizes communication and the people's capacity to listen and respond. God explicitly tells Moses that the people will listen to his voice (3:18: 'וְשָׁמְע֖וּ לְקֹלֶ֑ךָ'), instructs him to gather the elders and inform them of God's covenant (3:16-18), and documents that the people ultimately 'believed and listened' (4:31: 'וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ'). The appointment of Aaron as a spokesman underscores God's desire to facilitate dialogue with the people, not suppress their voices. There is no indication that the Hebrew people are discouraged from expressing their views.
